content.thinking:
I'm planning the design of a nine-tailed kitsune fox quadruped model, working out proportions like shoulder height and body length, and setting up a coordinate system with the floor and facing direction before building the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hips.

I'm defining the spine chain from hips to chest and the neck chain leading up to the head joint, then setting up the body as a swept sealed mesh with elliptical cross-sections along the spine path, attaching the neck and head as parented chains with their own radius profiles.

For the head, I'm planning out the skull and muzzle as scaled primitives, adding a jawed mouth, extruded ear shapes, and eye decals placed via surface projection onto the skull with mirrored positioning for symmetry, all oriented using the head joint's local forward/up frame.

Still defining the ear geometry...

Working out neck placement between shoulders and head, then setting up the leg bone chains with shoulder/hip anchors and paw targets, figuring out segment lengths so the limbs bend naturally for a digitigrade stance.

Four names matches hip, knee, hock, toe with hips as parent for both spine and hind chains. For leg sweeps I'm varying the radius along each segment and painting dark "sock" coloring below a height threshold to mimic fox stockings, using a custom paint function nested in a cel shader.

Attaching small sphere paws at each foot, bound to the final leg joint, with a few tiny cream claw spikes added at the toes for detail. For the nine tails fanning from the rump, I'm setting up each as a 4-joint chain.

Still writing tail curves...

Since there are only 9 tails, numbering stays unambiguous even with the "tail+index" naming scheme, so I'll keep it simple rather than switching to letters. Each tail chain should parent to a rump joint, with bases spread slightly along x using a sine offset so they don't overlap, and I'll sweep each chain into a tapered shape using its path for coloring.

I'm scattering fur tuft cards across each tail using a teardrop texture, going with a cream-to-orange gradient so the base and tip read differently without needing separate meshes. For the spirit flames orbiting the fox, I'm considering whether to build them as extruded outlines or simple glowing cards with a flame svg texture.

Going with double-sided card cutouts using a blue-teal outer and white-cyan inner flame texture: one pair crossing at each tail tip and six floating orbs circling the fox, all run through the glow effect since it accepts mesh arrays directly.

For positioning I'm framing each tail-tip flame off the chain's last point, nudging it upward slightly so it sits above the tip rather than through it. The fire gets its own glow intensity bump to make it pop.

Now I'm thinking about adding anime-style gold accessories — a filigree collar with a ring, tassel, and red magical beads wrapped like a shimenawa rope around the neck.

I'm sweeping a thin gold tube around the neck's mid-joint to form the collar ring, sizing the radius carefully so it hugs the neck rather than floating off it or clipping into it. I was planning to hang a glowing teal pendant at the front, but figuring out which side of the ring actually faces forward on a tilted neck is getting ambiguous, so I think I'll skip the ring-based placement and instead compute the pendant position directly from the neck's center.

Now I'm thinking through the kitsune-style details: a gold cord with tassels and maybe a red tie hanging from the pendant, plus red facial markings — cheek swooshes and a forehead diamond — applied as decals on the skull surface using the hit point and direction from the skull's surrounding geometry, alongside the anime-style eye decals positioned just above them.

Working out eye placement on the skull sphere, I'm settling on a narrow fox-eye shape with azimuth around ±38° and slight elevation for a forward-facing look, debating iris color between gold, cyan, and violet before leaning toward violet to tie into the spirit-flame theme. For the body, I'm setting up a cel-shaded fur coat with orange fur fading to a cream countershaded belly, adjusting the edge threshold and ink parameters for the fur shader.

For the overall palette, I decide against a classic white-and-red kitsune look and commit to golden-orange fur with cream chest, belly, and tail tips, dark sock markings, and red accent marks. I'm also planning a textured mane and chest ruff using card-based fur tufts scattered along the neck and cheeks, flowing downward and backward with moderate lean and bend, using cream-colored tuft textures to match the coat.

Still writing scatter filters and ear paint logic...

Now I'm thinking about gold rings around the tail bases, using the chain's path position to find points and tangents for sweeping circular bands, with tail radius interpolated along a profile function.

Tuning the taper function...

I'll skip extra tassel beads and gold accents to keep it simple, but I do need paws, claws, eyes, whiskers, eyebrow marks, and the nose defined. For the spine, I'm setting up a three-point chain resampled into a smooth path, rooted at the hips joint near the base of the torso.

Now I'm extending that chain forward: hips feed into spine1 at the same point, and the body sweep widens toward a rounded rear dome for the rump, with hindquarter thigh spheres attached at the hip joint for extra shape and painted with cel-style coloring. The chest and shoulders pick up from the spine path's last joint, positioning the shoulder blobs near the front end of the torso.

Continuing outward, the neck chain parents off the final spine joint and runs from the spine's end point up and forward in two segments with tapering sweep radii, connecting into a head joint positioned slightly above and ahead of the neck's tip. The skull is scaled to sit centered on that head joint while the muzzle extends forward from the skull along a short path.

Writing muzzle geometry and fur colors...

Adding small white teeth, then skipping interior mouth detail since the jaw stays closed. Now I'm placing eye decals on the skull surface using surface hit points, plus red brow swoosh markings mirrored on each side with small SVG paths.

Next I'm adding a forehead teardrop mark and cheek line decals, guarding against null surface hits before applying them. Then I'm extruding large anime-style ears from the head with a sharp pointed outline shape.

Working out the nine tail positions, fanning them by azimuth and elevation so the center tails sit higher and the outer ones angle outward, with each tail curving upward toward its tip.

Capping tail tip height around 1.9m so the fan stays proportional to the fox's 1m body, and checking that the sidemost tails spread wide enough (~1.6m fan width) without too much overlap between adjacent tails given their angular spacing.

I'm now setting up the tail skeleton chains with proper naming and parenting to the hips, then sweeping the tail geometry along each chain using a radius function, with round caps at both ends and a gradient-based paint applied per tail.

Writing flame SVG shape...

Now placing floating foxfire orbs around the fox at varied radii and heights, sizing them small so they create a scattered glowing effect without overwhelming the tails.

For the collar and pendant, I'm computing the neck position and tangent at the midpoint of the neck chain to orient the collar correctly, then writing a helper function to generate circular point rings perpendicular to that direction for the collar geometry.

Adding the pendant and tassels...

Now I want a gold crescent tiara on the forehead between the ears, built as an extruded lunate outline with sharp horn tips curving upward.

Working out crescent placement against the skull's curved surface—checking whether it protrudes forward enough without clipping fully inside, and considering tilting it backward slightly so the base sits embedded while the tips project outward.

I'm also planning a glowing red-magenta gem at the crescent's center, then shifting focus to body surface details: adding red fox-marking stripes along the flanks and legs using a custom paint pattern function layered over the base coat.

Still writing stripe logic...

Mapping out the joint hierarchy now: hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, legs, and the tail chains add up to 58 joints total. I'm setting tapered sweep radii for front and hind legs so they look naturally thicker near the body and thinner toward the paws, and sketching in chest ruff cards and sock-colored paint for the lower legs.

Rather than a hard color cutoff for the sock paint, I'm switching to a toothy fur-edge boundary between orange and sock colors, blended with ink shading for a more organic transition. I still need to nail down eye color, nose color, and a cream tone under the chin and jaw, plus figure out paw placement for ground contact.

Now I'm working out the hind leg geometry — setting ankle and paw positions so feet rest at ground level, then checking the hip-to-toe distance against segment lengths to make sure the hock bends naturally and the knee reaches forward correctly. I'm laying out the hind leg bone chain as hip, knee, hock, and toe joints for the sweep.

For the tail, I'm positioning the base embedded into the rear of the body near the hip cap, and for the body I'm defining the spine curve from hips to chest with a radius profile that widens toward the chest.

Now I'm placing the shoulder joints and front leg targets relative to body width, computing the leg segment lengths and bend direction for the elbow, and noting the neck ruff uses scattered geometry along the neck sweep.

Setting up the ruff scatter and tail tuft cards...

Now I'm checking imports needed from the codebase—THREE, builder helpers, frame, offset, rng, path utilities, limb for IK, paint, svg textures, toon kit pieces, and glow—making sure I only import what's actually used so there aren't unused-name errors, and confirming the limb function accepts vector arrays for its root parameter.

Writing a ringPts helper to generate ring points, then flame and tuft texture helpers using svg. I'm setting up the flame cards with crossed flow direction so they face correctly, and considering how to color paw sock parts using a plain hex string.

Now I'm defining more flat color constants for gold and red elements, setting up whisker rods as separate parts, and writing the SVG decal for a teardrop-shaped facemark positioned on the forehead with its own sizing and orientation.

Next I'm designing cheek and brow decals: curved swoosh strokes in red rendered as SVGs, positioning them mirrored on each side of the face with appropriate scale and alignment to the surface normal.

I'm also bumping up the eye size slightly for better proportion, and setting up the skull's base coat paint using a sphere geometry with head-shaped scaling, letting countershading give a cream underside near the chin.

Now I'm checking how Part's `around(HEAD)` and `.at()` methods handle null hits, then moving on to the tail bands—computing gold ring points along the tail path at t=0.2 using the tangent and radius function, sizing the band radius slightly larger than the tail's circumscribed polygon radius so it sits flush on the surface.

Adjusting the band offset and sides, I decide against adding a second band or tip bead, and instead focus on the tail's flame tip card frame positioned at the path's endpoint. I'm also setting up weight assignment for the flame cards so they bind to the nearest tail joint, and combining all tail flame cards into a single batched call. Finally I'm defining the TR tail radius function...

The hips joint is created first as root, owning no mesh itself, with hind thigh parts attached to the hind leg chain. Now I'm writing out the actual code with minimal typing, referencing joints directly.

Still writing joint hierarchy...
